_doc: Canonical cross-binding parity fixture (the NO-DRIFT guard). One file, run through every face (Rust core, Go-via-wasm, Python, TS). Each case names an op and its input envelope; every face must produce a byte-identical ok-JSON payload and an identical ok/err classification. A divergence is a CRITICAL drift bug. Inputs use the wire shape every binding shares: input_schema, default_presence, snake_case enum tags, {"pin":..}/{"constrain":{"enum":..}} arg policies. See SPEC.md and CLAUDE.md 'Binding parity & docs - NO DRIFT'.

cases._note: Rename over an UNBOUND base name: admitted, and the ok-payload comparison is what pins the rename into every face's merged policy. This case is also the only one here that can catch a STALE go/internal/wasmbin/lagom.wasm, because a pre-88cb040 blob classifies it err while the rust reference says ok (a status drift). Err cases cannot: the comparator compares only classification for err (parity/runners/compare/main.rs).
cases.name: merge_rename_overlay_admitted

cases._note: The sealing half: a base that already SET a rename is a bound, so redirecting it elsewhere is rejected by every face. Classification-only (see above), so this case guards cross-face agreement on the seal; it does not detect a stale blob.
cases.name: merge_rename_redirect_rejects

cases._note: UNKNOWN-KEY BLOCK (4 cases). Every case here carries a key the Policy model does not define. A face whose engine denies unknown fields classifies err; a face whose engine ignores them classifies ok on a policy that no longer means what its author wrote. So this block is also the WASM-STALENESS GATE the fixture set previously lacked: a stale go/internal/wasmbin/lagom.wasm classifies all four ok against the rust reference's err and the comparator reports a status drift. Each case is shaped so the stale engine's op actually SUCCEEDS -- an unknown key that merely produced a different err would be invisible, because the comparator compares only classification for err (parity/runners/compare/main.rs). THIS CASE: the lagom.toml spelling `default-presence` pasted into a wire policy. On an engine that ignores it the seal reverts to the Keep default and write_file survives projection -- a sealed sandbox downgraded to passthrough, with an ok.
cases.name: project_kebab_default_presence_rejects

cases._note: Singular `arg`. On an engine that ignores it the pin vanishes: `artifact` stays in the projected schema and the agent keeps setting it itself, while the projection still reads correct under audit.
cases.name: project_typoed_args_key_rejects

cases._note: Misspelled `presence`. On an engine that ignores it the tool falls through to default_presence and is dropped -- the opposite of the author's intent, with no diagnostic.
cases.name: project_typoed_presence_key_rejects

cases._note: `maximum` inside a range. On an engine that ignores it the bound parses as {min:1,max:none} -- a PARTIAL parse -- so limit=999 is admitted by a policy whose author capped it at 50. Half the bound enforced, and the call reads legitimate.
cases.name: rewrite_range_typoed_maximum_rejects

cases._note: MINT-SHAPE half of the unknown-key block. The four cases above bound `Policy` only; this one bounds the persisted mint shapes (MintRecord -> PolicySources -> UpstreamCommand), which no other case reaches. A refire case carrying `record` hands that on-disk shape across the same JSON boundary in every face, so the guard is compared rather than bypassed -- unlike `upstream_command`, which the Python and Node runners destructure into command/args/env and never pass whole. THIS CASE: singular `arg` in both recorded upstream commands. On an engine that ignores it `args` falls to its `#[serde(default)]` empty vec, refire returns ok, and the proxy launches the correct executable stripped of `--sealed` -- what RUNS changes, and the record still reads correct under audit. Everything else in the record is well-formed, so the err is attributable to the unknown key alone.
cases.name: refire_record_typoed_args_key_rejects

cases._note: DISCRIMINATION CONTROL for the case above: the same record with the key spelled `args`. Every face must classify it ok, so the sibling's err is attributable to the unknown key and not to some unrelated defect in the record's shape. Its ok-payload is also byte-compared, so this case doubles as a staleness detector on the refire path.
cases.name: refire_record_inline_ok
